paper_metadata.title: Additively manufactured Co–Cr–Ni multi-principal element alloys with excellent strength and ductility at room and cryogenic temperatures

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: Additive manufacturing (AM) can facilitate the design of novel multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs), with the CoCrNi system gaining prominence for its outstanding mechanical properties.

evidence.section: 2.2. Powder mixing and printing
evidence.quote: Elemental Co, Cr, and Ni powders, each with particle sizes in the 50–100 µm range, were procured and measured in the desired ratios, then mechanically mixed using ball milling to ensure homogeneity. A low milling speed of 100 rpm for 3 h and a low ball-to-powder ratio of 5:1 were employed

evidence.section: 2.2. Powder mixing and printing
evidence.quote: The optimised parameter set, ensuring stable, defect-minimized multi-layer deposition, included a laser power of 700 W, scan speed of 8 mm/s, powder feed rate of 7.54 g/min, hatch spacing of 0.3 mm, and a scan rotation of 67°.

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: In both alloys, multiple deformation mechanisms activated at 77 K, including dislocation slip-mediated mechanisms, twinning, and ε-martensite formation.
